sections.title: Positive outlook
sections.content:
Vocabulary for expressing hope and positivity about the future:
• optimistic — hopeful about the future. She's optimistic about her career prospects.
• aspire — direct hopes towards achieving something. He aspires to become a surgeon one day.
• ambitious — having a strong desire to succeed. She set ambitious targets for the coming year.
• anticipate — expect or look forward to. We anticipate significant growth next quarter.
• promising — showing signs of future success. The early results look very promising.

sections.title: Negative outlook
sections.content:
Expressing worry or doubt about the future:
• pessimistic — expecting the worst. Economists are pessimistic about the recovery.
• dread — anticipate with great fear. She dreads the thought of public speaking.
• inevitable — certain to happen. Change is inevitable in any growing organisation.
• uncertain — not able to be relied on. The future of the project remains uncertain.
• sceptical — not easily convinced. Many people are sceptical about the new plan's success.

exercises.question: Someone who expects good things to happen is:
exercises.explanation: Optimistic means hopeful and confident about the future.

exercises.question: Something that is certain to happen is:
To strongly fear something in the future is to:
exercises.explanation: Dread means to anticipate with great fear or anxiety.

exercises.question: Not easily believing claims is being:
exercises.explanation: Sceptical means not easily convinced; having doubts.

exercises.question: To direct your hopes towards a goal is to:
exercises.explanation: Aspire means to direct one's hopes or ambitions towards achieving something.

exercises.question: Signs of future success make something:
exercises.hint: It looks like it will succeed.
exercises.explanation: Promising means showing signs of future success.

exercises.question: Someone who always expects the worst is:
exercises.explanation: Pessimistic means tending to see the worst aspect of things.

exercises.question: To expect something to happen, often positively, is to:
exercises.explanation: Anticipate means to regard as probable; expect or predict.
